episodes.title: The Gwinnett County Cult Case That May Be Falling Apart | What Happened to Sehee Cho?
episodes.description:
Thirty-three-year-old Sehee Cho left South Korea and traveled to Georgia in the summer of 2023. According to investigators, she hoped to recover from a traumatic experience and begin a new chapter in her life. Instead, authorities allege that she became trapped inside a Lawrenceville home with people who referred to themselves as the “Soldiers of Christ.”

Police allege that Sehee was called “Number Five,” confined in a basement containing a miniature church, subjected to beatings, denied adequate food and exposed to ice-water initiation rituals. Weeks later, her severely malnourished body was found wrapped inside the trunk of a Jaguar parked near Jeju Sauna in Duluth, Georgia. The spa was not accused of involvement.

The case became even more complicated when one of the original defendants claimed that he had also been imprisoned and tortured. Then, in January 2026, a Gwinnett County judge dismissed several of the most serious charges against six defendants because of deficiencies in the indictment—creating a stunning new legal twist.

Tonight on Viral Crimes with Jocelyn, we are breaking down:

Why Sehee came to Georgia
The alleged “Soldiers of Christ” initiation
The Lawrenceville basement
The disturbing cellphone evidence described in court
How Sehee’s body was discovered
The seven people originally accused
The defendant who says he was another victim
The possible effort to recruit another woman
The indictment problem and dismissed charges
What may happen next

This presentation discusses allegations contained in police statements, testimony, court proceedings and news reports. Criminal defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court. The dismissal of charges is not the same as a jury finding that an alleged event did not occur.

Viewer discretion advised: This program discusses confinement, starvation, physical abuse, death and disturbing allegations.
